history.title: A reconstructed history
history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: His family is put with the village at the portage, at the camping place of Chicago, three leagues from the fort (about thirty men, Co-wa-bee-mai their chief in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring, and lives the year round in the lodges by the river below the fort, where most families came only to trade and went to their wintering grounds.
He is of the Wolf gens (Mo-ăh′), and his children are of it after him.

He is here with his wife Swift Bear Woman, his wife's mother One of the Fish, his son White Wolf (16), his daughter Spring Wolf Pup (12), his son Morning Wolf Pup (8) and his daughter Small Wolf Pup (5).
He fishes the river from the bank below the lodges in the warm months, and in the fall goes after ducks and geese in the marshes.
When the bands gathered at Chicago in August he was already here, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets with the rest when the goods were handed out.

card_evidence.quote: The Indians continued to come and go on their nomadic excursions according to their habit
card_evidence.claim: Before 1812 the Potawatomi came and went at Chicago as a habit.

card_evidence.quote: while in this vicinity they lived in their wigwams near the river, their favorite camping place being at a point on the south bank
card_evidence.claim: Their usual camping place was the State Street creek on the south bank.

card_evidence.quote: who were anxious to sell them supplies in exchange for the furs brought in by them
the Indians also brought in quantities of maple sugar put up in birch-bark packages
card_evidence.claim: Furs and maple sugar brought in for trade.

card_evidence.quote: carried with them to their wintering-grounds, to be brought back in the spring, when they returned to make their corn-fields
card_evidence.claim: Most families left for winter hunting grounds and came back in spring (Juliette Kinzie's own observation, March 1831); this family is put as staying, which is ours.

card_evidence.locator: pt. II, ch. II (VI, the right of bestowing names) and ch. VI (the gentes, notes 170 and 172)
card_evidence.quote: These names either proclaimed by their signification the gens to which they belonged, or were known as such by common reputation.
card_evidence.claim: how a reconstructed name is made

card_evidence.quote: At the camping place of Chicago, three leagues from the Lake Michigan, or Chicago Fort, is a village of Pottawatomies, Chippewas and Ottawas, of about thirty men.
card_evidence.claim: the village at the portage, the band these cards are put with (reconstructed)

card_evidence.quote: the tribes there assembled to amount of 500 warriors 179 women & children
Their number of warriors was between four and five hundred, mostly of the Potawatamie nation
we were taken back to their encampment near the fort, and distributed among the different tribes
card_evidence.claim: the prisoners brought back to the camp
